name: UpperTheory.V.PropA.xUnip
source: ∀ (k Ω : Type) [Field k] [NumberField k] [Field Ω] [Algebra k Ω] [IsAlgClosure k Ω] (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (N : ℕ)
(U : Subgroup (G k Ω)) [U.Normal], IsClosed (U : Set (G k Ω)) → Module.Finite ℤ_[l] (Xinf l N U) →
∀ γ ∈ levU l U 1, Unip (xRep l N U γ) := by
intro k Ω _ _ _ _ _ l _ N U _ hU hfin γ hγ
refine dualUnip l (Dinf l N U) (dRep l N U γ⁻¹) (xRep l N U γ) hfin (fun x φ => xRep_apply l N U γ x φ) fun φ => ?_
obtain ⟨n, -, hn⟩ := (dinfNil k Ω l N U hU φ.1 φ.2).2 γ⁻¹ (inv_mem hγ)
have key : ∀ (m : ℕ) (ψ : Dinf l N U), (((dRep l N U γ⁻¹ - 1) ^ m) ψ).1 =
((funRep ℤ_[l] (QZ l) (cycU l U) γ⁻¹ - 1) ^ m) ψ.1 := by
show: Let U be a closed normal subgroup of the absolute Galois group of a number field with chosen algebraic closure. Fix ℓ prime and N natural. If the corresponding module X∞ is finitely generated over the ℓ-adic integers, every level-one element γ of U acts on X∞ unipotently modulo ℓ.
strategy: Identify the action on the dual as precomposition by the action of the inverse element on D∞. The Kummer local-nilpotence input acts pointwise on the underlying discrete module, so the dual unipotence criterion applies.

steps.claim: Let $\gamma$ be in the level-one subgroup, so its inverse also belongs to that subgroup. On $X_\infty=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(D_\infty,\mathbf Q_\ell/\mathbf Z_\ell)$ the action of $\gamma$ is precomposition with the action of $\gamma^{-1}$ on $D_\infty$. The dual unipotence criterion therefore uses finite generation of $X_\infty$ and pointwise nilpotence on $D_\infty$. For each character $\varphi$ the discrete Kummer nilpotence result, using closedness of $U$, provides an exponent $n$ at which the ambient difference operator for $\gamma^{-1}$ kills its underlying function.

steps.claim: Write $T$ for the action of $\gamma^{-1}$ minus the identity on $D_\infty$ and $A$ for the corresponding difference on all functions. With $i$ the inclusion of allowed characters into functions, $i(T^m\psi)=A^m i(\psi)$ for every $m,\psi$ because the discrete action is the restriction of the function action.

    intro m

children.claim: Induction on $m$ proves that forgetting the character conditions commutes with taking each power. The identity cases coincide, and each successor uses $i(T\psi)=A i(\psi)$.
At $m=0$, $i(T^0\psi)=i(\psi)=A^0 i(\psi)$ since both zeroth powers are identity maps.
If $i(T^m\eta)=A^m i(\eta)$ for every $\eta$, take $\eta=T\psi$. Restriction of the action gives $i(T\psi)=A i(\psi)$, hence $i(T^{m+1}\psi)=A^{m+1}i(\psi)$.

steps.claim: The Kummer exponent for $\varphi$ gives $A^n i(\varphi)=0$. By the power comparison and injectivity of $i$, $T^n\varphi=0$. This pointwise nilpotence supplies the dual criterion, so some power of $\gamma-1$ maps $X_\infty$ into $\ell X_\infty$.
